title: Temperance Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: Temperance upright: balance, patience; reversed: extremes or impatience. Love, work, advice, Waite's 1911 text and the 1909 card. Draw it for your question.
image_alt: Temperance, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a winged angel in a white robe pours a stream between two gold cups, one foot in a pool, with a path leading to mountains and a yellow light.
capsule: Temperance, card XIV, stands for balance, moderation, patience and harmony: the slow blending of things that seem opposed. Reversed, the mix tips into excess, extremes or hurry. It is a steadying card, and it would rather you did not force the pace. Because the parts are settling into place without strain, a yes-or-no question gets a yes upright.

blocks.heading: What is on the Temperance card?
paragraphs: A tall angel in a white robe stands at the edge of a pool and pours a stream from one cup into another. Waite describes "a winged angel, with the sign of the sun upon his forehead", and then corrects himself: "I speak of him in the masculine sense, but the figure is neither male nor female" (p. 124). What flows between the cups, he says, is "the essences of life", passed "from chalice to chalice" (p. 124).

One foot rests in the water and the other on the bank, which for Waite shows "the nature of the essences" (p. 124). On the 1909 card the wings, in red and dark tones, spread almost from edge to edge and are the largest shapes on the card. The hair is yellow, a gold disc sits on the forehead, and on the breast is a square with a triangle inside, Waite's "square and triangle of the septenary" (p. 124). XIV is printed at the top, and tall yellow flowers rise from the reeds on the right.

On the left a path climbs from the water toward far mountains. Waite writes of "a direct path" up to the heights, and above it "a great light, through which a crown is seen vaguely" (p. 124). On the 1909 card that light is a yellow glow over the peaks.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about Temperance?
paragraphs: The upright list is practical: spending with care, keeping to the middle, running things well, making room for others. The reversed list opens with churches and the priesthood, a side of the card Arcana Diary does not read, and closes with things that refuse to mix: disunion, unfortunate combinations, competing interests.

Waite found the name puzzling at first sight. He wrote that on the surface "the entire symbol has no especial connexion with Temperance" (p. 24), and later explained why it is called so "fantastically": under its rule the figure "tempers, combines and harmonises the psychic and material natures" (p. 127).

blocks.heading: What does Temperance mean upright?
paragraphs: Temperance in its upright position describes balance found slowly: blending two sides of a situation, two needs, or two parts of yourself until they work together. It tends to appear when you are tempted to swing hard one way, and it offers the middle path instead.

Moderation here does not mean standing still. The angel keeps the stream moving between both cups; nothing stops and nothing is wasted. Patience is the working tool: steady, small adjustments rather than one dramatic fix. The result is rarely spectacular, but it holds. Modern readings also link the card to healing in the emotional sense: recovery after a hard stretch, taken one calm step at a time.

The card also favors combining what already works instead of starting from zero: an old skill with a new setting, rest with effort, your needs with someone else's. There is a calm sense of purpose in it as well: blending patiently because you know what the mix is for. Worth asking: where am I trying to rush something that only works at its own pace?

blocks.heading: What does Temperance mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, Temperance shows a mix out of proportion: excess, too much of one thing and too little of another, or impatience with a process that cannot be hurried. You might catch yourself going to extremes, all or nothing, acting in haste with no setting in between.

The end of Waite's reversed list, disunion and competing interests, points the same way: parts that pull against each other instead of blending. Reading this side as excess and hurry is modern, not Waite's.
This imbalance does not call for a full overhaul. Pick one area that has tipped too far and bring it a little back toward the center; the rest often follows.

blocks.heading: What does Temperance mean in love?
paragraphs: Pouring slowly from cup to cup, the angel sets the pace for love: a gentle middle ground. When you are getting to know someone, it suggests a calmer pace: no racing ahead, and your own life kept in balance while you do.
Where there is a partner, the card speaks of harmony and a good fit, of give and take that flows: where you could soften, and where you need to stay true to what you need.
If the card is reversed, it can mean discord, or a rhythm that swings between very close and very distant. What small change would bring it back toward the middle?

blocks.heading: What does Temperance mean for work and money?
paragraphs: Long projects, mixed teams and combined skills suit this card: it prefers steady progress to bursts of overtime, blending a team's ideas rather than pushing one, and it can point to a role where you are the one who brings people together.

Waite's list for this card opens with "economy, moderation, frugality" (p. 285), and the modern money meaning stays close to it: a balanced budget, steady finances kept through moderate spending and saving, no swings to extremes.
The reversed card can show up where work or spending has turned into all or nothing: overspending, or money going out faster than it comes in.

blocks.heading: What is Temperance's advice?
paragraphs: Pick one area of life where you tend to overdo or underdo things and move it a notch toward the middle. Temperance does not ask for a new regime, only one small correction you can keep up. After a while, notice how the rest of the mix responds.

blocks.heading: Is Temperance a yes or no card?
Temperance as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: The go-between is the role Temperance often gives a person: someone patient who finds the workable middle and helps different sides meet. In your own case, it shows your ability to stay steady while things settle. On the feelings side, the card speaks of calm, steady affection: ease and harmony with someone, a sense that the two of you fit and can take things at an unhurried pace. Reversed, feelings swing between extremes, close one day and distant the next, or turn impatient and push too fast.

pairs.text: Balance in motion. Keep juggling, but decide which demand gets the steady pour first.
Two people meeting halfway. Give and take in proportions that feel fair to you.
Friction meets patience. Look for the idea that can hold the clashing views together.
Gentle power and an even pace. Quiet persistence will carry you further than force.

blocks.heading: Temperance or The Star?
paragraphs: Both cards show a figure pouring water with a foot in it. In The Star the figure kneels: "Her left knee is on the land and her right foot upon the water", and she pours from two ewers onto "sea and land" (p. 136). Temperance stands and passes the stream between two cups held in the air. The Star is hope and renewal after a hard stretch; Temperance is the patient work of blending, a balance built step by step. One restores, the other adjusts.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about Temperance
paragraphs: Where in my life am I swinging between too much and too little?
What two things am I trying to blend, and what pace do they need?
What small adjustment could I keep up without strain?

faq.q: Is Temperance a good or bad card?
faq.a: Quietly good. It backs patience, steady effort and the knack of bringing opposites together. Forced results are what it warns against. Because it is so calm, it is easy to overlook in a spread, yet it often marks the point where things begin to settle.

faq.q: Does Temperance mean I have to give something up?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The word suggests abstaining to many people, but the picture shows mixing, not refusing: the liquid moves from cup to cup. Waite himself wrote that, on the surface, the image has no special link with the name (p. 24). The card asks for proportion, which sometimes means less of something and sometimes more.

faq.q: What number is Temperance in tarot?
faq.a: Temperance is card XIV, number 14 of the Major Arcana, placed between Death and The Devil. Waite gives it the same number, 14, in his survey of the trumps in Part I (p. 24).

faq.q: Does Temperance mean he loves me?
faq.a: In its traditional meaning, Temperance describes affection that is gentle and lasting rather than dramatic: patient care that grows step by step and wants the relationship to work for both people. It is a card of harmony, not of grand gestures. Reversed, the same affection is read as uneven, warm and then cool.

waite.quote: Economy, moderation, frugality, management, accommodation. Reversed: Things connected with churches, religions, sects, the priesthood … also disunion, unfortunate combinations, competing interests.
